notable_absence.finding: The page states that when no data type is set, the Search Service 'automatically assigns a field data type', and for dynamic type mappings specifically 'the Search Service automatically assigns data types to all fields in the type mapping' - but it never states WHAT algorithm or rule governs that automatic assignment (e.g. does a numeric-looking string become 'number' or 'text'?). No relation could be minted for this because the object of the assignment rule is not itself named or enumerated anywhere on the page.

cross_component_finding: This page is the first in the corpus to enumerate the Search field-data-type list as its own closed catalogue (text, number, datetime, boolean, disabled, geopoint, geoshape, ip, vector, vector_base64) - minted as search:field-data-type-enum. 'disabled' is explicitly marked legacy ('This field data type is deprecated. It's included for compatibility only.') with no replacement named, which is worth flagging alongside the existing retainedForLegacyCompatibility predicate shape, though I did not assert that relation here since the page names no specific superseding construct (retainedForLegacyCompatibility's range expects 'the modern construct that supersedes it' or a version era, neither of which this page states for 'disabled').
